Integration / Development note

Integration starts with the contract.

Before the connector or endpoint, questions about data, responsibilities and failures deserve an answer.

By Sergio Hernández3 November 2026
In this note
  1. Understand the business operation
  2. Make the exchange explicit
  3. Design the error path too
  4. Test the complete process

Connecting two systems means more than getting a request to respond. An integration needs an agreement about what the information means, who may request it and what happens when the exchange fails.

Understand the business operation

Start by describing the process: what triggers it, which system owns the data and what the person using it needs. A useful integration preserves that meaning from beginning to end.

A Power Apps application, Power Automate flow and .NET API can take part in the same process. The choice of components depends on their responsibilities and the constraints of the environment.

Make the exchange explicit

The contract describes fields, types, identifiers, optional values and expected responses. It should also clarify how dates are represented and how errors are communicated.

Distinguish a validation failure from an operation that cannot be completed at that moment. That difference lets an interface or automation respond coherently.

Design the error path too

A service can become temporarily unavailable and a request can be repeated. Before adding retries, understand whether repeating the operation might create a duplicate or perform an action twice.

An operation identifier and contextual logging help trace the exchange across systems. Credentials and data that the log does not need should stay out of it.

Test the complete process

Beyond a successful response, review incomplete inputs, missing permissions, unexpected responses and external service failures. Test how the process continues and what the user is told.

Documenting the contract and error-handling decisions makes the integration easier to evolve when one of the systems changes.

Putting it into practice

Define the meaning of the data, permissions and failure behaviour before considering a connection between systems complete.
